implementable_controller_requirements: One outer unit aggregate service cgroup contains preparation, all hashing, worker fork/exec, observer, archive/receipt finalization and cleanup. Any systemd control subgroup remains beneath that same aggregate ancestor.
Do not launch a sibling transient service from the main controller. Keep the outside host request a literal manager activation transport, not a custom hash/observer/result workflow.

Systemd v255 realizes the unit cgroup for every command spawn. Main receives EXEC_PASS_FDS; Pre and StopPost do not. StopPost uses EXEC_CONTROL_CGROUP. Test ancestry rather than assuming identical leaf membership.

Treat each command mount namespace as fresh. Private tmpfs preparation contents cannot be assumed to survive into Main or StopPost. A single Main which performs preparation itself avoids that particular handoff, while manager limits must already apply.
Use fixed fail-if-existing unit identity or another reviewed job lock which covers preparation and cleanup. A lock first acquired in Main does not protect Pre.
Enumerate start, running, stop-post and final termination timeouts. RuntimeMax alone and a rate quota alone are not complete cumulative wall/CPU limits.

Preserve finite partial evidence on controller loss; missing terminal receipt/counters remains unknown or failure, never automatic success. A process inside its own populated cgroup cannot attest that the whole cgroup is already empty.

storage_assessment.tmpfs: size/nr_blocks bounds allocated tmpfs data pages; nr_inodes bounds inodes and xattr consumption. Kernel metadata accounting and charged RAM are distinct and must be stated. New mounts and actual exhaustion remain untested by this review.
storage_assessment.sealed_memfd: A fixed number of pre-sized memfds with verified GROW and SHRINK seals can supply a kernel-backed volatile export length boundary. WRITE sealing can freeze final contents. Seals are volatile and are not a persistent ext4 quota.
storage_assessment.shared_ext4_fixed_FDs: Existing per-file FSIZE, default-allow allocation-bypass filter, bounded FD count and post-hoc st_blocks checks are useful defenses but do not establish a dedicated hard capacity accounting for shared filesystem metadata/journal or early inode/directory provisioning.
storage_assessment.persistent_output_missing_gate: Before any persistent provisioning, require a measured block/inode quota with reviewed accounting scope OR a reviewed truly fixed-capacity backing filesystem/volume whose creation and all writers are within the envelope.
storage_assessment.no_privilege_alternative: FUSE support is installed, but no suitable ready writable bounded-image filesystem driver was found. A custom FUSE/libext2fs design would require independent implementation, security/source review and exact bounded tests; available libraries alone are not proof.
storage_assessment.prohibited_automatic_recovery: No sudo, host remount, quota enablement, package install, security-flag removal or resource expansion was attempted or is recommended as an automatic next action.

primary_sources.supports: Per-command cgroup preparation and conditional descriptor passing.
StopPost has EXEC_CONTROL_CGROUP and no EXEC_PASS_FDS.
Tmpfs size/block and inode limits; distinguish volatile storage from persistent capacity.
Irreversible whole-inode GROW/SHRINK/WRITE seals are supported only on special volatile files.

verdict: Persistent hard-capacity gate remains BLOCKED. Proceed with actual controller engineering and bounded evidence only; never convert volatile diagnostic or post-hoc accounting into full storage PASS.
